surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the autoregulated growth of MgTe during atomic layer epitaxy (ALE), where Mg and Te are alternately pulsed onto the surface. The growth is self-regulated, with a periodic stabilization of the surface after each pulse, leading to a consistent growth rate of approximately 0.7 ± 0.1 MgTe monolayers per ALE cycle. The process includes the incorporation of Mg atoms and Te atoms, with the surface reconstruction playing a role in stabilizing the growth.
